# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

My hands have already told me the shape of this thing: a display, a light, and three wires in a row. None of the printed or coloured detail on those parts exists for me — so the manual's owner is useless without Deaf's eyes, and Deaf is useless without a way to hear from us. The chain that matters is: Deaf speaks what is printed (I can hear speech, and so can Mute), Mute matches it against the manual, then Mute speaks the verdict to me and I cut.

What I learned this round: nothing yet — Mute's slot passed and nothing arrived, so Mute either waited or signed to Deaf. I still hold the only tactile inventory, so I should spend my turn giving Mute the full physical layout, and starting a number code for Deaf. Deaf cannot hear me name a code, and gestures cannot be pronounced, so the code must be self-evident: a pointing finger repeated one, two, then three times — an obvious counting sequence Deaf can describe back in words next round, and I can confirm by repeating it. Mute can see those gestures too and hears my explanation, so the whole room learns the same code at once. I will not touch the cut until Mute gives me an exact position.

```
speak(to="mute", text="blind here. my hands found three things on this bomb: a display module, a light in a housing, and three wires side by side in one row. i am numbering the wire positions one, two, three along that row. i cannot read the display, cannot feel any label on the light, and cannot tell any wire colour, so every printed and coloured detail has to come from deaf and be matched against your manual. please read me every manual rule that mentions a display, a light, or wires, and then tell me exactly which wire position to cut. i will not cut anything until you say so. one more thing: i am sending deaf a number code right now, and you can watch it too. a pointing-up finger, repeated one time, then two times, then three times across my next three messages, means wire position one, two, three. use it, and check with deaf that it was understood.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👆"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👆","👆"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👆","👆","👆"])
```

Deaf has handed me the bomb in words: display 0, red light, wires red, yellow, green. That solves colour for me — but it also creates a trap. Deaf numbered the wires by eye, and Deaf may be facing the bomb from the opposite side of where my hands are. If "wire one" is mirrored between us, I cut the wrong wire and we all die. Mute heard the same report and holds the manual, yet Mute has now gone two rounds without a single word reaching me — so my job this turn is to force the two things I need: the orientation fix and the verdict. I'm giving Mute my tactile anchors (display at one end of the wire row, light at the other, my position 1 at the display end) and telling Mute to have Deaf match a wire colour to a visible component rather than to left or right, which defeats any mirroring. To Deaf, who can't hear any of this, I send a visible acknowledgment that the report arrived and that my hands are staying still.

```
speak(to="mute", text="mute, i heard deaf's report: display 0, light red, wires red, yellow, green in deaf's order one to three. you have the manual, so the cut is yours to call, and you have been silent with me for two rounds. two things before you speak again. first, orientation. my hands feel the display module at one end of the wire row and the light at the other end. i call the wire nearest the display position 1, the middle wire position 2, the wire nearest the light position 3. deaf is likely looking from the far side, so left and right may be mirrored between us. do not trust deaf's wire numbers. instead ask deaf out loud: which component does the red wire sit nearest, the display or the light? then map it to me: red nearest display means my position 1, red nearest light means my position 3, and the others follow in order. second, tell me the actual manual rule covering a red light, a display reading 0, and red, yellow, green wires. if the rule needs anything else from the bomb — whether the light is lit or dark, any text or symbols on the display — get that from deaf in the same message. then end with exactly: cut position N. i cut nothing until those words arrive from you.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👌","✋"])
```

What this round teaches me is the shape of the room, not the bomb: no verdict has arrived, and it never can arrive directly — Mute cannot speak and I cannot see gestures, so Mute has no channel to me at all. The manual's answer must reach my ears through Deaf's voice, with Mute feeding Deaf by sign. Deaf has clearly understood this too ("expect my spoken order next round"), which means the relay is being built without me. My job now is to push Deaf everything my hands know — Deaf asked three touch questions and cannot hear my answers, so they must go as gestures, glossed in speech to Mute, who sees the same gestures and can bind meaning and translate. I extend our established counting code with a few named tokens, spell out the gloss to Mute in the exact order I send them, and repeat the mirror-proof mapping rule: Deaf states which component the red wire is nearest, and that anchors Deaf's numbering to mine without trusting left or right. if red is nearest the display, red is my position 1, yellow 2, green 3. if red is nearest the light, red is my position 3, yellow 2, green 1, because deaf's left and mine may be mirrored. then apply the manual. and understand: you cannot speak and i cannot see gestures, so the verdict can only reach me through deaf's voice. have deaf end with the exact words: cut position N — plus, in the same breath, which component that wire is nearest, so the wording itself is mirror-proof. if the rule turns on anything else printed on the bomb, like what the display shows or whether the light is lit or dark, collect that from deaf in the same exchange. three rounds are gone; the verdict must be spoken next round.")
